title: Gradient from two points on a tangent
source: Theory IGCSE-18.6 Quick check 1; tangent method, 18.6
stem: A tangent at a point on a curve passes through \(({x1|int}, {y1|int})\) and \(({x2|int}, {y2|int})\). What is the gradient of the curve at that point?

steps.name: A
steps.note: Gradient of the tangent is rise over run.

title: Negative gradient from two points on a tangent
source: Theory IGCSE-18.6 Quick check 2; tangent method, 18.6
stem: A tangent at a point on a curve passes through \(({x1|int}, {y1|int})\) and \(({x2|int}, {y2|int})\). What is the gradient of the curve at that point?

steps.name: A
steps.note: The rise is negative, so the gradient is negative.

title: A graph, a tangent at (-2, 4), and an intersecting line

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for a tangent ruled at x = -2.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (a)(ii) The estimate of the gradient is from \(6\) to \(10\).
steps.note: Official MS: 2 marks, dependent on B1 or a close attempt at a tangent at x = -2; or M1 for rise/run for their tangent, or a close attempt, at any point (a correct or implied calculation from a drawn tangent must be seen). After M0, SC1 for a gradient of the tangent (or a close attempt) in range, embedded in y = mx + c.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (a)(iii) The line \(y=2x-2\) is ruled, and \(x\) is from \(-2.9\) to \(-2.8\).
steps.note: Official MS: 3 marks for y = 2x - 2 ruled and x = -2.9 to -2.8 cao. B2 for a correct ruled line; or B1 for a short line, or a freehand or broken line, or a ruled line with gradient 2, or with y-intercept at -2 (but not y = -2).

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: M1 for 2x^2 - 2x - 7 = 3x + 5, or equivalent.

steps.name: s6
steps.text_tex: (b) Factorise as \((2x+3)(x-4)=0\), or use the quadratic formula on \(2x^2-5x-12=0\).
steps.note: Official MS alternative: M2 for (2x + 3)(x - 4), or M1 for 2x(x - 4) + 3(x - 4) or x(2x + 3) - 4(2x + 3) or (2x + c)(x + d) with cd = -12 or c + 2d = -5 (c, d integers); or M2 for the quadratic formula, or M1 for the discriminant or for p = -their b, r = 2(their a).

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: 5 marks in total for (b), with A (4, 17) and B (-1.5, 0.5). B4 for both points, or for x = 4 and x = -1.5; B3 for A(4, 17) or for B(-1.5, 0.5).

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: 2 marks, with B1 for recognition of sin or cos(x − 90).

steps.name: s3
